clues.stem: Every scorching Paris July, why does the wrought-iron Eiffel Tower grow up to six inches taller than it measures in January?
clues.ahaFactoid: Heating 7,300 tons of puddle-iron latticework makes molecules wiggle farther apart—leaning the tower slightly away from the sun too!

clues.stem: Traditional Japanese origami starts from a flat sheet with zero glue or cuts—what geometric shape do classic origami squares always start as?
clues.ahaFactoid: Washi folding paper is cut squarely so diagonals and corners meet predictably—letting hundreds of intricate models emerge from crisp squares!

clues.stem: Why did young Michelangelo carve his towering 17-foot David out of a notorious giant marble block left rotting in Florence for 40 years?
clues.ahaFactoid: Agostino di Duccio chipped an awkward hollow right through the middle in 1464—until 26-year-old Michelangelo brilliantly worked around the flaw!

clues.stem: Why did Claude Monet build an arched Japanese footbridge and willow-rimmed pond at Giverny before painting his giant Water Lilies?
clues.ahaFactoid: Monet proudly said his garden itself was his greatest masterpiece—hiring six gardeners just to keep petals clean and vibrant!

clues.stem: How did ancient Roman engineers shield 50,000 cheering Colosseum spectators from blistering Mediterranean noon sun?
clues.ahaFactoid: Detachment sailors from Rome’s naval base manned 240 wooden masts to rig the "velarium" retractable canvas shade overhead!

clues.stem: Look at Grant Wood’s pitchfork-toting Iowan farmer and daughter: why does the window behind them share the painting’s title "American Gothic"?
clues.ahaFactoid: Wood spotted that charming little Carpenter Gothic farmhouse in Eldon, Iowa and asked himself what kind of sturdy folks belonged inside!

clues.stem: Peer closely at Edward Hopper’s moody 1942 diner masterpiece Nighthawks: what eerie architectural detail traps the four midnight patrons inside?
clues.ahaFactoid: Whether by design or sleek glass framing, Hopper left zero street door in the curved corner window—deepening wartime city isolation!

clues.stem: Contrary to the myth he sold zero art alive, Van Gogh DID sell one oil painting at an 1890 Brussels show—who bought The Red Vineyard?
clues.ahaFactoid: Belgian Impressionist painter Anna Boch paid 400 francs (~$2,000 today) to encourage Vincent—just months before his death!

clues.stem: How does Rome’s nearly 2,000-year-old Pantheon concrete dome stay standing without steel rebar—and why does rain fall straight onto its marble floor?
clues.ahaFactoid: Roman builders swapped heavy travertine at the base for airy volcanic pumice near the open 27-foot oculus sky-eye—with subtle floor drains below!

clues.stem: How did the word "Impressionism" start in 1874—with a proud manifesto, or with a sarcastic Parisian critic’s mockery?
clues.ahaFactoid: Journalist Louis Leroy snickered that Monet’s misty harbor "Impression, Sunrise" was less finished than rough wallpaper—so the rebels adopted the insult!

clues.stem: Before shimmering with real 24-karat gold leaf in Vienna’s The Kiss, Gustav Klimt spent months studying gleaming 6th-century mosaics in which Italian city?
clues.ahaFactoid: Staring at Ravenna’s golden San Vitale basilica tiles inspired Klimt’s dazzling "Golden Phase" combining modern Vienna style with Byzantine shimmer!

clues.stem: In Vermeer’s paintings, tiny round dots of white paint shimmer across woven bread baskets and brass studs—what optical phenomenon do they mimic?
clues.ahaFactoid: Called "circles of confusion" (optical bokeh) in out-of-focus lenses, those pearly paint dots strongly suggest Vermeer peered through a camera obscura!

clues.stem: Hollywood cinematographers still name a classic portrait shadow setup after Rembrandt—defined by a crisp lit triangle landing where?
clues.ahaFactoid: Illuminating half the face plus one sharp upside-down triangle of light on the shadowed cheek delivers instant 17th-century psychological drama!

clues.stem: Building Florence’s massive dome without wooden centering scaffolding underneath, Filippo Brunelleschi locked curved courses with what clever brick pattern?
clues.ahaFactoid: Every few horizontal rings, vertical herringbone ("fishbone") bricks wedged the growing masonry shell tight so inward courses couldn’t slide into midair!

clues.stem: ELEMENTARY ART ROOM: Mixing cyan, magenta, or red-yellow-blue gives endless hues, because you only start with three [ _____ ] colors!
clues.ahaFactoid: Printers mix Cyan-Magenta-Yellow inks while TV screens blend Red-Green-Blue light—two completely different primary trios!

clues.stem: HARBOR ARCHITECTURE WIRE: Perched over Sydney’s sparkling Bennelong Point, Jørn Utzon’s gleaming white ceramic roof [ _____ ] billow like yacht sails!
clues.ahaFactoid: Utzon cracked the engineering puzzle by slicing all ten sweeping concrete vaults cleanly out of the exact same geometric sphere!

clues.stem: 1964 MANHATTAN STUDIO: Lining East 47th Street walls in crinkled aluminum and silver paint, Andy Warhol dubbed his velvet-rope hub The [ _____ ]!
clues.ahaFactoid: Inside The Factory, Warhol silkscreened Marilyn and Elvis portraits assembly-line style while rock stars and filmmakers filmed screen tests!

clues.stem: 2018 AUCTION SHOCK: Seconds after Sotheby’s gavel slammed at $1.4 million, Girl with Balloon slid down through hidden blades inside its own [ _____ ]!
clues.ahaFactoid: Wait—the shredder jammed halfway down, accidentally creating a brand-new conceptual piece that later resold for over $25 million!

clues.stem: 1886 PARIS SALON: Rejecting broad brushstrokes, Georges Seurat and Paul Signac dotted pure color specks side-by-side to pioneer [ _____ ]!
clues.ahaFactoid: Up close La Grande Jatte looks like glowing confetti; step back ten feet and your optic nerve blends green grass and purple shadows!

clues.stem: 1930 ARCHITECTURAL DIGEST: Celebrating Detroit optimism, William Van Alen crowned the Chrysler Building’s terraced stainless spire with winged radiator [ _____ ]!
clues.ahaFactoid: Even the 31st-floor gargoyles were sculpted directly after 1929 Plymouth winged radiator hood ornaments jutting above Lexington Avenue!

clues.stem: EDO PRINT BULLETIN: Hokusai and Hiroshige flooded 1800s Tokyo stalls with vivid hand-carved cherry [ _____ ] prints of actors and Mount Fuji!
clues.ahaFactoid: Affordable ukiyo-e sheets even wrapped porcelain shipped to Paris—blowing away Impressionists and Post-Impressionists alike!

clues.stem: 8TH-CENTURY CONSTANTINOPLE: Ordering mosaic portraits chipped off church walls in a fierce century-long split, Emperor Leo III sparked the [ _____ ] Crisis!
clues.ahaFactoid: From Greek "image-breaking," Iconoclasts vs Iconophiles battled fiercely until mosaics triumphed again in 843 CE!

clues.stem: Look at the blood-orange fjord sunset swirling behind a wide-eyed skull-like figure clutching both cheeks—where is the character standing?
clues.ahaFactoid: Edvard Munch remembered walking along Oslo’s Ekeberg hill road with two friends when the sky suddenly turned blood-red and nature seemed to shriek!

clues.stem: Zoom onto the golden pocket watch lying face-down in Salvador Dalí’s The Persistence of Memory: what creepy-crawlies swarm its metal lid?
clues.ahaFactoid: Since childhood, Dalí used swarming black ants as an eerie shorthand for decay—while the limp clocks melt across Catalonia’s rocky coast!

clues.stem: Walk around Auguste Rodin’s brooding bronze Thinker: which part of his own body props his heavy resting chin?
clues.ahaFactoid: Look closely next time: his right elbow crosses onto his LEFT knee while the back of his right hand presses under his chin—curling his whole torso!

clues.stem: Standing delicately on the scalloped edge of a giant ocean shell blown shoreward by winged winds, Botticelli’s Venus covers herself with what?
clues.ahaFactoid: Wait—a nymph on the right rushes forward holding a flower-patterned pink cloak ready to wrap Venus the moment she steps ashore!

clues.stem: Look past the glowing blue-and-yellow turban in Vermeer’s Girl with a Pearl Earring: what fills the space right behind her shoulder?
clues.ahaFactoid: Conservators discovered that dark backdrop originally shimmered with a rich translucent green glaze over dark charcoal—now darkened with age!

clues.stem: Step inside Diego Velázquez’s Las Meninas: right at the rear wall’s center hangs a tiny glowing mirror reflecting whom?
clues.ahaFactoid: Because the King and Queen stand right where YOU stand viewing the canvas, Velázquez painted himself looking straight at royalty—and you!

clues.stem: Inspect the round convex mirror hanging between Jan van Eyck’s 1434 Arnolfini couple: tiny painted roundels around its frame show what scenes?
clues.ahaFactoid: Ten jewel-like millimeter scenes of Christ’s Passion ring the glass—with two tiny witnesses (including Van Eyck!) reflected inside the bedroom!

clues.stem: Stare diagonally down along the carpet in Hans Holbein’s 1533 The Ambassadors: what distorted gray smear snaps into sharp focus from the side?
clues.ahaFactoid: That stretched anamorphic reminder of mortality ("remember you must die") hovered by a staircase landing—snapping crisp as guests walked past!

clues.stem: GALLERY KLAXON! Three of these Mona Lisa facts are 100% TRUE—which stubborn rumor is completely BOGUS?
clues.ahaFactoid: Mona Lisa really sits on thin poplar wood, hung in Napoleon’s bedroom, and vanished in 1911—no diamond frame!

clues.stem: STUDIO KLAXON! Three of these Bob Ross facts are TRUE—which cheerful claim is BOGUS?
clues.ahaFactoid: Ross learned wet-on-wet oil painting from PBS host Bill Alexander in Alaska—never met Picasso! And yes, he really raised pocket squirrel Peapod!

clues.stem: MONUMENT KLAXON! Three of these Eiffel Tower facts are TRUE—which tourist claim is BOGUS?
clues.ahaFactoid: Eiffel’s tower is famously wrought "puddle iron" latticework brushed in 60 tons of bronze-brown paint—zero concrete tower!

clues.stem: HARBOR KLAXON! Three of these Statue of Liberty facts are TRUE—which claim about 1886 is BOGUS?
clues.ahaFactoid: Liberty glowed shiny penny-brown in 1886 before Atlantic salt air oxidized her 3/32-inch copper plates into iconic sea-foam green!

clues.stem: VATICAN KLAXON! Three of these Sistine Chapel facts are TRUE—which Hollywood myth is completely BOGUS?
clues.ahaFactoid: Wait—Michelangelo actually stood upright on custom bridge scaffolding AND hated oils for ceilings; he painted buon fresco on wet lime plaster!

clues.stem: ATELIER KLAXON! Three of these Picasso facts are TRUE—which gallery myth is completely BOGUS?
clues.ahaFactoid: Picasso was obsessed with bulls and peace doves—drawing hundreds of minimalist lithographs and even winning UN peace fame with his 1949 Dove!

clues.stem: MUSEUM KLAXON! Three of these ancient sculpture facts are TRUE—which textbook myth is BOGUS?
clues.ahaFactoid: Classical marble gods and temples blazed with cinnabar red, Egyptian blue, and gold leaf—rain and zealous Victorian scrubbers stripped them white!

clues.stem: PIGMENT KLAXON! Three of these bizarre art-supply facts are TRUE—which claim is completely BOGUS?
clues.ahaFactoid: Prussian blue was accidentally synthesized in a 1704 Berlin chemistry lab from potash and iron salts—never scraped off oak trees!

clues.stem: Color physics check: when you mix red, green, and blue spotlights together on a white theater stage, what bright color appears in the center?
clues.ahaFactoid: Mixing light is ADDITIVE (RGB -> White), whereas mixing paint is SUBTRACTIVE (absorbing wavelengths until dark brown/black)!

clues.stem: Sculpture showdown in Florence! Who cast a sleek bronze David wearing a jaunty laurel-trimmed shepherd hat nearly 60 years before Michelangelo’s marble giant?
clues.ahaFactoid: Carved around 1440 for the Medici courtyard, Donatello’s gleaming youth became the first freestanding nude bronze since classical antiquity!

clues.stem: Canvas framing 101: turning a rectangular painting or phone screen TALLER than it is wide is universally called what orientation?
clues.ahaFactoid: Named after upright head-and-shoulders paintings vs wide horizon views—even laser printers still call tall pages Portrait!

clues.stem: Material check! When Auguste Rodin sculpted famous versions of The Thinker for outdoor plazas like Paris and Cleveland, what metal did foundries cast?
clues.ahaFactoid: Unlike Michelangelo’s marble David, Rodin’s clay models went to foundries for gleaming bronze casts—over 25 official life-size casts exist worldwide!

clues.stem: Italian plaster showdown: which mural technique bonds pigment chemically into WET lime plaster so it outlasts centuries?
clues.ahaFactoid: Leonardo’s Last Supper flaked terribly precisely because he experimented with dry-wall tempera/oil instead of true wet buon fresco!

clues.stem: Temple-column spotter: which ancient Greek column sports spiral ram-horn scrolls ("volutes") curled neatly on top?
clues.ahaFactoid: Easy eye check: Doric wears a plain cushion cap, Ionic wears twin scroll curls (think "I" = Eyes/scrolls), and Corinthian bursts with acanthus leaves!

clues.stem: 17th vs 18th century mood: which dramatic style uses stormy dark shadows and theatrical tension, vs pastel garden swings?
clues.ahaFactoid: Caravaggio and Bernini’s Counter-Reformation Baroque packs thunderous chiaroscuro drama; French Rococo floated into Fragonard’s candy-pink picnics!

clues.stem: Printmaker’s grain clash: does a traditional Japanese woodblock cut carve the image ONTO raised wood ridges or INTO sunken metal channels?
clues.ahaFactoid: Woodblocks are relief prints (ink rolls across standing wood lines), whereas copper engravings wipe ink off flat surfaces leaving ink deep inside grooves!
